messages:
sara (CS): Hey team — customer reports streaming SSE from our /v1/streams endpoint drops after ~20s in Safari (mobile + desktop). They see partial output, then client reconnects and gets 401 or an empty stream. Repro steps attached from them.

mike (eng): Can you paste the customer's raw headers + timeline? Is this only Safari?

sara (CS): They said Chrome is fine. Safari reproduces every time. Copied their debug: 
```
GET /v1/streams?id=abc HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Accept: text/event-stream
Connection: keep-alive
Cache-Control: no-cache
```
Response (first stream chunk): 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private
X-Cache: HIT from cdn.example
<...some event frames...>
```
Then after ~20s we see a `304` from the edge on a preflight/ping (they have a client-side preconnect/timing probe) and Safari shows the connection going into stalled state. After reconnect the new request is missing Authorization (edge stripped it on 304?) and server returns 401.

ashley (infra): Interesting — CDN 304 midstream is suspicious. Some CDNs/edges treat preflight or revalidation differently and can drop or rewrite Authorization for cached 304 responses unless Vary: Authorization is set.

mike (eng): Also note Safari's EventSource behavior: if it sees a preflight or intermediate 304, the underlying TLS/TCP might try to reuse the connection and the browser's keep-alive heuristics + our chunking can interact poorly. Could you get the full edge logs and the exact timestamps?

sara (CS): Pasted what they gave: timestamps 2024-11-10T14:02:17Z -> initial connect, 14:02:37Z -> partial pause, 14:02:38Z -> edge 304 revalidate, 14:02:38Z -> client reconnect 401. They also use a global CDN with aggressive caching.

jon (support): Quick repro script we used locally (mac Safari 17.1):
```
# openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -quiet
curl -v -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?id=test\" --no-buffer
```
We saw the stream cut at ~18-22s. When we disabled CDN (bypassed origin) the issue disappears.

mike (eng): OK that isolates CDN interaction. Two immediate hypotheses: 1) CDN is serving a cached 304 for a conditional revalidate request and dropping Authorization on the cached response path, 2) CDN sets `Cache-Control: max-age` or `must-revalidate` on some intermediate object and then collapses the stream. Also look for `Vary` header missing (Authorization). If Vary: Authorization missing, CDN might respond with a cached 304 that doesn't preserve auth.

ashley (infra): Can we ask the customer / CDN team to dump the full request/response pairs around the 304? Specifically we want to see: the conditional request (If-Modified-Since / If-None-Match), the 304 response headers from CDN, and whether the edge rewritten the Connection/Transfer-Encoding. If the edge returns 304, it should not be used midstream for SSE.

sara (CS): I asked them to enable debug logs from the CDN and sent recommended curl with `-D -` to dump headers. Awaiting logs.

mike (eng): Short-term workaround for customer: 1) add `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform` on client -> instruct CDN to not revalidate SSE responses, 2) set `Vary: Authorization` on our SSE responses so CDN won't reuse cached copies across tokens, 3) optionally switch to cookie/query token for the stream (less ideal). Also recommend switching to `Connection: keep-alive` and ensure the CDN is configured to pass-through chunked responses and not to compress or buffer SSE (no gzip transform).

sara (CS): Customer tried adding `Cache-Control: no-cache` on client fetch, still saw 304 path on the edge. They said the CDN has an edge rule that aggressively normalizes preflight/conditional reqs.

jon (support): Could we change response headers server-side to `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform, private` for SSE endpoints? That should prevent edge caching altogether.

mike (eng): Yes — we can push a change to the SSE handler to emit:
```
Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform, must-revalidate, private
Vary: Authorization
```
And add a small signpost header: `X-Stream-Mode: sse` so infra can create a CDN rule that bypasses caching/transform for that path.

ashley (infra): I'll open a ticket with CDN support to clarify why they return a 304 midstream and whether they strip Authorization on revalidate paths. We should provide them with an example trace and request IDs. If they can't guarantee pass-through, we'll need to block caching at the CDN layer for `/v1/streams`.


deploy-bot: deploy started: origin change (sse headers) -> staging -> canary -> 3/3 nodes.

mike (eng): After deploy, can someone test with the customer's exact token flow and Safari? We should also get them to try latest eventsource polyfill as a mitigation; some polyfills re-open connections more gracefully and send auth correctly on reconnect. However it's better to make server/CDN correct.

sara (CS): Customer confirmed they can test tonight — asked if we can provide a canary URL to validate.

ashley (infra): Canary URL: https://canary-api.redwood.example/v1/streams?trace=cdntest. Also asked CDN to disable any `If-Modified-Since`/`If-None-Match` revalidation for that path. Ticket ID: CDN-19872 (assigned).

jon (support): Follow-ups: ask customer to capture the Safari network panel & console when reproducing, include the request ID from our canary header `X-Request-Id` if present. Also advise them to try with a browser extension disabled (some extensions cause preflight traffic).

sara (CS): Noted. I'll update the customer with canary link + suggested headers and ask for logs.

mike (eng): Longer term: add instrumentation to expose `X-Stream-Mode` and `X-Edge-Cache` in our logs for every SSE connection so we can quickly detect when an edge is rewriting. Also add an automated test that runs Safari + a mock CDN that issues 304 midstream to ensure regressions don't happen.

sara (CS): Thanks. Marking as high-priority until customer validates canary. Will follow up with logs. :thumbsup:
